data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.question: emotion
sections.summary: A strong feeling such as joy, love, fear, or anger that affects your thoughts and behaviour.

senses.definition: a strong feeling such as happiness, sadness, fear, or love, that affects how you think and behave
examples: The film was so moving that it stirred up strong emotions.

answers.answer: Anger is a strong emotion.
Anger is strong emotion.
Emotion are important.

sections.question: enthusiasm
sections.summary: A feeling of great excitement and eager interest in something.

senses.definition: intense and eager enjoyment or interest in something; a strong feeling of excitement or energy about a subject or activity
examples: She approached every new challenge with great enthusiasm.

answers.answer: She showed enthusiasm for the project.
She showed an enthusiasm for the project.
Enthusiasm are important at work.

sections.question: excitement
sections.summary: A feeling of great happiness and eager anticipation about something enjoyable.

senses.definition: a feeling of great happiness, eagerness, or anticipation, usually caused by something enjoyable that is happening or about to happen
examples: There was great excitement at school on the last day of term.

answers.answer: There was a feeling of excitement in the room.

sections.question: experience
sections.summary: Knowledge or skill gained by doing something or being involved in something over time.

senses.definition: knowledge, skill, or understanding that comes from direct involvement in or exposure to something over a period of time
examples: She has a lot of experience working with young children.

answers.answer: He has experience in teaching adults.
He has an experience in teaching adults.

sections.question: feeling
sections.summary: An emotion or physical sensation that you are aware of in your mind or body.

senses.definition: an emotion or physical sensation that you are aware of; the way something makes you feel inside
examples: He had a good feeling about the job interview.

sections.question: gift
sections.summary: Something that you give to another person, especially to celebrate a special occasion.

senses.definition: something that you give to someone, especially to show affection or to celebrate a special occasion; a present
examples: They gave her a gift to thank her for all her help.

answers.answer: She bought him a gift for his birthday.

sections.question: goal
sections.summary: Something that you want to achieve in the future; an aim or objective.

senses.definition: something that you want to achieve in the future; a specific aim, target, or purpose you are working towards

sections.question: insight
sections.summary: A deep and clear understanding of a person, situation, or subject.

senses.definition: the ability to understand something clearly and deeply; a piece of understanding gained about a complex situation or subject
examples: The course gave me real insight into how languages work.

sections.question: knowledge

sections.question: manner
sections.summary: The way in which something is done or the way a person behaves towards others.
